title: AWS CWI Training in San Francisco, CA: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Bay Area refinery, bridge, seismic steel and pipeline welders: corporate, online or one-to-one. Parts A, B and C covered.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in San Francisco: Six Days for Bay Area Refinery, Bridge and Seismic Steel Welding Inspectors
html:
The Bay Area asks a lot of its welds. Refinery piping along the Carquinez Strait runs hot and under pressure, bridge steel over the Golden Gate and the bay has to ride out earthquakes, and high-rise frames in San Francisco carry seismic connections that leave no room for sloppy fit-up. When something goes wrong here it tends to make the news, which is one reason owners, agencies and contractors around the bay take welding inspection seriously. Atlantis NDT offers a six-day (6-day) preparation course for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination, working through Part A Fundamentals, Part B Practical and Part C Code Application, in three formats: on site for an employer's group, online for individuals with an instructor on hand for questions, and one-to-one. AWS administers the CWI examination and grants the certification; Atlantis gets candidates ready and certifies no one. There is no Atlantis classroom in San Francisco, nor anywhere else in the Bay Area. Atlantis offices are in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India. To begin, send a San Francisco CWI exam prep enquiry.

How the six days work for a Bay Area candidate

Every day of the course lines up with something the exam tests. Days one and two cover the Fundamentals behind Part A: welding processes and heat input, AWS terms and definitions, joint design, welding and weld symbols, metallurgy, mechanical testing, discontinuities and their causes, the NDT methods and what each can find, calculations, safety and inspector ethics. Day three prepares you for the hands-on practical with gauges, measurement and procedure records. Day four is spent navigating the code book you picked for Part C. Day five is timed practice papers, and day six fixes weak spots and covers the run-up to the exam. The AWS CWI exam prep course page has the detail.

Corporate: for a refinery contractor, fabricator or inspection firm

An employer preparing several people can have the six days delivered at its own site, with the practical built around its own gauges and real welds and the code day pitched at the book the group will use, whether that is the ASME package for plant people or D1.1 and D1.5 for structural and bridge staff.

Online: for individuals fitting study around turnarounds and commutes

Individuals get a study plan built on the six-day outline, course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, with an instructor answering questions as they go. No sessions are timetabled, so study fits around turnaround shifts, bridge night work and long Bay Area commutes.

One-to-one: for a single candidate

Six days of sessions with the instructor for one candidate, either online or in person at a location agreed when booking, with all of the time spent on that person's needs.

The Bay Area welding economy, sector by sector

Welding inspection around the bay is spread across a few big sectors, several of which are changing fast.

Refining and fuels along the Carquinez Strait and in Richmond

The East Bay and Solano County have long been one of California's refining centers, home to Chevron's Richmond refinery and the plants around Martinez, Rodeo and Benicia. The picture is shifting. Valero told the California Energy Commission in 2025 that it might idle, restructure or cease operations at its Benicia refinery, and by February 2026 reports said all of the refinery's units had been idled ahead of closure. In Martinez, Marathon has converted its site to a renewable fuel facility, while the Martinez Refining Company suffered a fire in February 2025 that injured six people and halted operations for a time. For welding inspectors, fewer crude refineries means fewer turnarounds in total, but the plants that remain, and the converted renewable fuels units, still run maintenance, repair and turnaround work under ASME B31.3 and Section IX, with chrome-moly and stainless materials, preheat and post-weld heat treatment at the center of the job.

Bridges and seismic retrofit

Bridge steel is a defining part of Bay Area welding work. The Golden Gate Bridge, Highway and Transportation District is now retrofitting the suspension bridge itself, the last major phase of its seismic program: strengthening the main span and side spans, reinforcing both towers and the south tower pier, adding large steel plates at the tower bases, replacing expansion joints and installing energy dissipation devices. The first construction contract for that phase was awarded in October 2025 and is expected to take about six years, with work starting in 2026 and weeknight lane closures to match. In August 2026 the District moved to hire a firm for quality assurance inspection of the structural steel being fabricated for that contract at shops in Georgia and Alabama, a reminder that Bay Area bridge inspection often travels to wherever the steel is made.

State highway structures follow Caltrans requirements. Where Caltrans specifies welding to an AWS code, the contractor works under an authorized Welding Quality Control Plan with a qualified quality control manager and inspection staff, Caltrans must be able to witness quality control testing, and no permanent welding may start until the engineer has authorized the submittals. Steel bridge members are generally welded to AWS D1.5, read alongside the contract's special provisions.

High-rises and seismic building steel

San Francisco's towers, hospitals, labs and transit facilities use structural steel welded to AWS D1.1, with seismic force-resisting systems that carry additional requirements under the AWS D1.8 seismic supplement and the AISC seismic provisions. The city has a cautionary example close to home. After cracks were found in two steel girders at the Salesforce Transit Center in 2018, the transit authority's consultants reported in 2019 that the weld access holes had not been ground before welding, a step that would have removed small cracks, and that several layers of fabricator, contractor and quality assurance inspection had missed it. The lesson for any CWI is that a skipped preparation step is a welding inspection failure even if the finished weld looks fine.

Ship repair and the waterfront

Ship repair in the bay has contracted. Mare Island Dry Dock in Vallejo announced at the turn of 2026 that it would close permanently after losing a large Coast Guard repair contract for the icebreaker Healy, affecting more than 80 staff. At the same time Solano County cities have passed resolutions supporting shipbuilding and the county has set up a working group on the subject, so the region's marine future is still being argued over. For now, marine welding inspection around the bay is a smaller niche than refining, bridges or buildings.

Pipelines, utilities and laboratory construction

Gas transmission and distribution pipelines across Northern California bring API 1104 work on new construction, replacements and integrity repairs. Biotech and life sciences campuses on the Peninsula and in the East Bay add stainless process and utility piping, much of it orbital-welded and inspected under the owner's specifications, with ASME Section IX governing procedures and welder qualifications. Water, wastewater and transit agencies keep their own capital programs running alongside.

Who hires CWIs around the Bay Area, and what they look for

  • Refinery maintenance and turnaround contractors. They need inspectors who know Section IX and B31.3, can track welder qualifications against each joint and can manage preheat, PWHT and hardness records under pressure.
  • Owner and operator QA groups. Refineries, utilities and transit agencies keep inspectors to oversee contractors, review weld records and audit fabricators.
  • Steel fabricators and erectors. Shops and field crews working to D1.1 and D1.5 need in-house QC, and Caltrans work brings formal welding quality control plans that name the people responsible.
  • Special inspection and testing firms. Permitted building projects in San Francisco and the surrounding cities rely on special inspectors for structural welding, and those firms hire CWIs.
  • Source inspection firms. As the Golden Gate steel shows, owners hire inspectors to watch fabrication at out-of-state shops, which suits CWIs who are willing to travel.

What links these roles is accountability. Bay Area owners have seen what happens when inspection layers assume someone else checked, and they want inspectors who record what they actually verified.

Choosing the Part C code for San Francisco and Bay Area work

Part C is open book, and you choose the book. AWS offers D1.1 for structural steel, API 1104 for pipelines, D1.2 for aluminum, D1.5 for bridges, D15.1 for railcars and locomotives, D17.1 for aerospace fusion welding, the ASME pairing of Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. Bay Area candidates usually decide between four:

Your main workPart C bookWhy it suits the Bay Area
Refinery, renewable fuels, power and process piping; biotech utilitiesASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3Qualification variables plus piping examination and acceptance, the daily language of plant work
Bridges, highway structures, bridge fabrication shopsAWS D1.5The bridge welding code behind Caltrans and toll bridge work
High-rises, labs, transit buildings and general structural steelAWS D1.1The base structural code for building steel and special inspection
Gas transmission and distribution pipelinesAPI 1104Pipeline welding procedures, welder qualification and acceptance standards

The exam uses the edition AWS specifies, which may be older than the one on your current project, so match your study copy to your application. Background: ASME Section IX, ASME B31.3, AWS D1.5, AWS D1.1 and API 1104.

The AWS San Francisco Section and Bay Area welding colleges

The AWS San Francisco Section, part of AWS District 22, is the local section for Bay Area welders and inspectors. Its fall 2026 program included a welding student night at Chabot College's welding department in October, with a guest speaker and virtual welding demonstrations, and a November section meeting at Las Positas College's welding department with the AWS national president as guest speaker. Those meetings are where you meet QC managers, working inspectors and educators, hear which contractors are staffing up, and find colleagues who can confirm your welding history for the AWS application.

The section's choice of venues also points to where many local welders train. Chabot College in Hayward and Las Positas College in Livermore both run welding departments, and the pipe trades, boilermakers and ironworkers train welders through their apprenticeships around the bay. AWS lets recognized education reduce the years of experience the CWI requires, and a school or apprenticeship record makes the experience you claim easier to verify. These programs are part of the Bay Area's training pipeline and are independent of Atlantis.

Booking the CWI exam from San Francisco

AWS QC1, the 2016 edition with its amendment, governs the CWI examination, and AWS requires a score of at least 72% on each part. Part A is 150 questions on fundamentals. Part B combines practical tasks with tools and specimens that AWS supplies and 46 questions. Part C is open book, around 50 to 65 questions on your chosen code. AWS sends a single consolidated score report.

Parts A and C are taken on computer at a Prometric test center, booked with the eligibility code in your AWS confirmation letter. Part B needs more planning, because AWS runs the practical only at its own seminar and examination locations on dates it sets. Check the current AWS schedule for the nearest session in California and apply early enough to make its deadline; depending on dates, the practical may mean a trip out of the Bay Area. AWS publishes its examination fees on aws.org, and the CWI exam cost planner helps with the wider budget, including time off and travel.

Studying around turnarounds, night closures and commutes

Bay Area work patterns make steady study hard. Refinery turnarounds bring weeks of long shifts, bridge and highway work often runs at night to keep lanes open by day, and many inspectors spend hours a day crossing bridges themselves. The online format is built for that: take the fundamentals in quieter weeks, read on public transit if that is how you commute, send questions to the instructor whenever they come up, and keep the timed practice papers for the last couple of weeks before your Prometric appointments.

For Part C, practise finding things quickly in your book rather than reading it cover to cover: acceptance criteria, qualification ranges, preheat tables. For Part B, measure real welds with fillet gauges, an undercut gauge and a bridge cam gauge until the readings are second nature. The Practical NDT welding workshop simulator adds browser-based practice on inspection steps, and the WPS, PQR and WPQ guide helps with the procedure questions.

Corporate: six days at a Bay Area employer's facility

Corporate delivery runs the six days at the employer's own premises, whether that is a contractor's yard near the refineries, a fabrication shop or an inspection firm's office. The practical day uses the company's own gauges and real welds, from welder test coupons to production cut-outs, so measurement practice matches the work those inspectors accept. The code day can be split for a mixed group, for example plant staff on the ASME package and structural staff on D1.1 or D1.5.

Scheduling usually works around turnarounds, bridge closures or project milestones. Each candidate still applies to AWS individually, meets the eligibility and vision rules individually and books their own exam; an employer can organize support but cannot apply for anyone.

One-to-one sessions for a San Francisco candidate

With one-to-one, a single candidate has six days of sessions with the instructor, online or in person at a location agreed when booking. It works well for a refinery pipefitter who knows B31.3 in practice but has never sat a timed code exam, a bridge ironworker heading into QC, or an engineer who needs the hands-on measurement skills Part B demands. The time follows that candidate's weak areas from start to finish.

Eligibility and the vision record for Bay Area applicants

AWS links the experience requirement to education. With a high school diploma you need five years of welding-related work; with a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology, one; other schooling falls between, and less schooling means more years. The work must involve welded products, such as fabrication, construction, maintenance, repair or inspection, and it must be verifiable, with AWS making the final decision. AWS also requires a Visual Acuity Record showing near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with or without corrective lenses, plus a color perception test, completed by a qualified practitioner within the period AWS allows before your exam. Candidates short on years can start with the AWS Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI). The full table is on the CWI exam prep course page, and the CWI requirements guide explains more.

After the CWI: career paths in the Bay Area

AWS keeps a CWI valid for nine years, with renewals at the third and sixth years and recertification at the ninth. Bay Area inspectors usually build from there in one of these directions.

  • Senior and lead roles. Inspectors who go on to run a contractor's welding quality program or an owner's inspection group often aim for the AWS Senior CWI; see the Senior CWI pathway. AWS endorsements widen the codes you are recognized on.
  • NDT methods. Plant, bridge and building work all use ultrasonic, magnetic particle and penetrant testing of welds. Performing those tests needs method training, logged experience and certification by your employer under its written practice. Atlantis teaches VT, MT, PT and UT on courses built around ASNT SNT-TC-1A; see NDT training in San Francisco, UT Level 2, MT Level 2 and VT Level 2, and the Practical NDT page for the Bay Area.
  • Source and owner-side inspection. CWIs with bridge or plant experience move into source inspection at fabricators and owner's representative roles on capital projects.

For a side-by-side of the main credentials, read CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II and the CWI results by exam part. For local services, see weld inspection services in San Francisco and ultrasonic testing in San Francisco.

Other West Coast CWI pages and a San Francisco quote

Candidates elsewhere on the West Coast can read the CWI exam prep pages for Los Angeles, San Diego, Portland and Las Vegas.

For a quote, tell us how many people want to prepare and which format suits, summarize each candidate's education and welding work, list the Part C book they plan on, and for corporate delivery give the site location, the gauges and sample welds available and any turnaround or closure dates to avoid. Use the San Francisco CWI enquiry form.

faq.q: Is the Atlantis CWI course taught in a San Francisco classroom?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in San Francisco or elsewhere in the Bay Area. Candidates take the six-day course online with an instructor answering questions, as one-to-one sessions online or in person at a location agreed when booking, or as a corporate course at their employer's facility. See the outline.
The American Welding Society. AWS administers the examination, scores it and issues the CWI. Atlantis prepares candidates for the exam; AWS has not approved, accredited or endorsed the course.

faq.q: Which Part C code should a refinery inspector in the East Bay choose?
faq.a: Most choose the ASME package of Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, because refinery and renewable fuels piping is built and repaired to those documents. See ASME Section IX.

faq.q: I work on Caltrans bridge projects. Which book fits?
faq.a: AWS D1.5, the bridge welding code, read alongside the contract's special provisions. Caltrans work also runs under a Welding Quality Control Plan, so expect to work with formal QC documentation. See AWS D1.5.

faq.q: Where do Bay Area candidates take the CWI exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are computer-based tests booked through Prometric with your AWS eligibility code. Part B, the practical, is run by AWS at its own seminar and examination locations on fixed dates, so check the AWS schedule for the nearest California session and plan for possible travel.

faq.q: Can a turnaround contractor have the course run at its yard?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format puts the full course on your premises, works with your own gauges and cut-outs, and is scheduled to stay clear of turnarounds. Each candidate still applies to AWS individually. Send an enquiry.

faq.q: Is the one-to-one format available in person in the Bay Area?
faq.a: Yes. The one-to-one option gives one candidate six days with the instructor, either online or face to face at a location settled when booking. With no Atlantis venue in the area, the location is set for each booking.

faq.q: Are the practice questions copied from AWS exams?
faq.a: No. The questions and timed papers are written by Atlantis from the topic areas AWS publishes, and Atlantis has no window into the AWS examination.

faq.q: Does refinery or bridge ironwork count toward the experience requirement?
faq.a: It can, if it was welding-related work on welded products and you can document it with dates, employers, the codes you worked to and someone who can confirm it. AWS decides what qualifies; see CWI requirements.

faq.q: What can I add after the CWI?
faq.a: Many Bay Area inspectors add NDT methods. Atlantis teaches VT, MT, PT and UT on SNT-TC-1A-based courses, after which the employer certifies you under its written practice. See NDT training in San Francisco.
